sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same OR1N1-3×FLAG construct, in which a 3×FLAG tag is fused to the protein's C-terminus (after residue 311). The authoritative topology landmarks place the entire C-terminal tail (residues 289–311) in the intracellular compartment. OR1N1 is a canonical class-A GPCR (olfactory receptor) with an extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–24) and an intracellular C-terminus; the 3×FLAG tag therefore faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface. No ledger line reports any tag insertion at an extracellular position (N-terminus, ECL1 78–95, ECL2 163–194, or ECL3 259–269). Because the ledger provides no evidence for an extracellular tag on OR1N1, zero sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: 3×FLAG fused to the C-terminus of full-length OR1N1 in a lentiviral construct; topology landmarks place residue 311 (and the entire 289–311 tail) in the intracellular compartment, so the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
